item.research_question: What are the long-term oxidation mechanisms and kinetics of a novel refractory high entropy alloy (NV1) at 1000 °C and 1100 °C over an unprecedented duration of 200 hours, and how does the formation of a CrTaO4-based oxide influence its resistance compared to existing literature?
item.material_system: NV1 alloy (Al17.6Si2.9Ti5.4Cr25.2Nb15.2Mo20.3Ta13.4 at%); as-cast microstructure contains Mo-rich BCC dendrites, Cr-rich hexagonal phase, and Al-rich tetragonal phase.
item.processing_route: Cold crucible levitation melting of high purity elemental raw materials (>99.9 wt%) to cast a 1.1 kg cone-shaped ingot; samples machined by electrical discharge machining and ground to 1200 grit; isothermal oxidation conducted in flowing dry air using a thermogravimetric analyser (SETARAM TAG 24-18S) and muffle furnace.
item.test_conditions: Isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C and 1100 °C for up to 200 hours in flowing dry air; microstructural characterization performed at intervals of 1, 12, 40, 50, 100, and 200 hours.
key_findings: At 1000 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 6.53 mg/cm², following an exponential dependence throughout the entire duration due to the inability to form a dense protective oxide layer.
At 1100 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm², showing three stages of parabolic dependence associated with the formation of a protective CrTaO4-based oxide layer.
The external oxide layer at both temperatures consisted primarily of CrTaO4-based oxide with dispersed Al2O3 and Cr2O3, but neither Al2O3 nor Cr2O3 formed continuous layers.
At 1000 °C, the oxide layer was porous with large volume defects caused by heterogeneous oxidation among chemically different regions (Mo-rich dendrites vs. Cr/Al-rich interdendritic regions).
At 1100 °C, the CrTaO4-based oxide layer was denser and more homogeneous, resulting from enhanced diffusion kinetics that allowed for the formation of a continuous barrier.

TiN particles (approx. 1.5 μm) formed preferentially within the Mo-rich dendritic regions in the internal nitridation depth (IND), while AlN particles were found in the internal oxidation depth (IOD).
The CrTaO4-based oxide at 1100 °C contained up to 7 at% Al and 2.2 at% less Cr compared to the oxide formed at 1000 °C, indicating a non-stoichiometric nature that accommodated metallic atoms.

The weight gain at 1100 °C (4.03 mg/cm²) indicates NV1 is one of the most oxidation resistant RHEAs compared to literature data to-date, outperforming AlCrMoNbTi, (AlCrMoNbTi)0.99Si0.01, and AlCrMoTaTi.
item.mechanism: At 1000 °C, insufficient kinetics prevented the formation of a dense CrTaO4-based oxide, leading to heterogeneous oxidation, volume defects, and exponential weight gain driven by external oxidation and nitridation. At 1100 °C, enhanced diffusion kinetics allowed for the homogeneous growth of a denser CrTaO4-based oxide layer which acted as a barrier to inward oxygen and outward element diffusion, resulting in parabolic kinetics; however, Mo evaporation from the OL/IOD interface in Stage II temporarily accelerated oxidation before Stage III slowed it down via further CrTaO4 formation.
item.limitations: The study notes that while the CrTaO4-based oxide provided protection, it could not fully prevent the ingestion of oxygen and nitrogen, leading to internal oxidation and nitridation. Additionally, the presence of the CrTaO4-based oxide might hinder the rapid formation of a protective Al2O3 layer by solutioning outward-diffusing Al atoms.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the nature of the CrTaO4-based oxide needs to be carefully examined in future studies, and that the influence of nitridation on RHEA properties is an important subject for further investigation.
quotes: At 1100 °C, mass gain curve showed two parabolic dependences associated with the formation of protective CrTaO 4 -based oxide layer and the weight gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm 2 , which indicates that it is one of the most oxidation resistant RHEAs comparing to literature data to-date.
At 1000 °C, the inability to form dense CrTaO 4 -based oxide layer resulted an exponential dependence of weight gain throughout 200 hours.
We believe that CrTaO 4 -based protection layer and Si addition may be important for future development of RHEA against oxidation and nitridation.
